title: Support fibers split into equal-cardinality slices
statement: Let $u$ be a word of length $n$ over a finite alphabet $\alpha$, let $S$ be a set of coordinate positions, and let $i$ be a position with $i \notin S$. For every symbol $a \in \alpha$ with $a \ne u_i$, the words in the support fiber of $u$ over $\{i\} \cup S$ — those differing from $u$ at exactly the positions in $\{i\} \cup S$ — whose entry at position $i$ equals $a$ are exactly as many as the words in the support fiber of $u$ over $S$, that is, the words differing from $u$ at exactly the positions in $S$.
hypotheses_covered: u is a word of length n over the finite alphabet α
S is a set of coordinate positions
i is a position with i ∉ S
a is a symbol with a ≠ u_i
replaced:
For $i \notin S$ and any alternative symbol $a \in \mathrm{choices}(u,i)$, the slice
$\{v \in \mathrm{supportFiber}(u,\{i\}\cup S) : v_i = a\}$
has the same cardinality as $\mathrm{supportFiber}(u,S)$.
